rv.q: But at its heart, this remains a play about family – how they love each other, fight with one another, and ultimately how they come together in times of crisis. Katrina Lindsay’s set design is a behemoth.

British productions of Chekhov are usually light on laughter and heavy on the tragedy of the situations they portray, but the most striking fact of Fall's production is that for all the piercing drama that unfolds is how much genuine humour it finds.
